transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I’m here because... honestly, everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just, you know, a matter of standard paperwork and missed payments. But I know for a fact that the bank, the loan servicer, and even people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. 

And it's funny I mention my job, because I'm a floor supervisor in retail, and just yesterday I had to write up this new cashier, Chloe, because she keeps leaving the security tags on the expensive coats. I swear, they don't train anyone right anymore. I have my associate's degree in business, so I try to tell the district manager how we could streamline the onboarding process so people actually know what they're doing, but he never listens to me. He just brushes me off. 

Just like how everyone brushes me off about my house. No amount of papers they try to show me changes what I’ve been seeing for almost two years now. They are all in on it to get me out.
Have you ever heard voices, whispering, or other sounds when no one was around?

Voices? No, I don't hear things that aren't there. I mean, if there's whispering, it's because people are actually whispering, like the loan officers at the bank. But no imaginary voices or anything like that. 

Actually, speaking of hearing things, our store intercom has been making this awful static noise for three weeks now. I put in a work order for it, and corporate just completely ignores it. It's like they want us to be miserable. I finally ended up bringing in my own little Bluetooth speaker just so we'd have some music up by the registers, because otherwise it's just dead quiet. And you know how awkward that is when a customer is just standing there staring at you while the receipt prints? Especially when the machine jams. Chloe jammed it twice on Tuesday because she yanked the paper before it actually cut. I had to show her, again, how to open the dispenser and reset the roll. It's just exhausting. 

But anyway, what were you asking? Oh, right, voices. No, just normal people talking.

An outside force? Like someone controlling my body or my thoughts? No, definitely not. I'm in complete control of myself. If I wasn't, I wouldn't be able to keep everything running at the store. 

Honestly, it feels like I'm the only one who *is* in control sometimes. Just this morning, I had to completely redo the endcap displays in the seasonal aisle because the overnight crew just dumped the new stock wherever it fit. They didn't even follow the planogram. I swear, the night manager, Rick, doesn't even look at the floor plan. He just wants to get out of there by 6 AM. And I’ve tried telling the district manager—again, with my business degree, I know how visual merchandising is supposed to drive sales—but it’s like talking to a brick wall. 

It’s just like the bank. They think they can just move things around and push me out of my house without me noticing. But I’m paying attention. I see exactly what they’re doing. But no, no outside forces controlling me. Just me, trying to keep everything from falling apart while everyone else plays their little games.

{"intent": "Assess for a pervasive, lifelong pattern of interpersonal mistrust to differentiate paranoid personality disorder from delusional disorder.", "question": "Outside of this situation with your house,

Outside of the house situation? No, I mean, I'm generally fine. When the foreclosure stuff isn't actively happening, I still get up every single day, go to work, supervise my team, handle the schedules, deal with customer issues... I take care of myself. 

Honestly, the customer issues take up half my day anyway. Just yesterday, this woman was screaming at me because she tried to return a blender without a receipt, and it wasn't even a brand we sell! I had to pull up the vendor list on the tablet to prove it to her, and she still threatened to call corporate. People just feel so entitled, you know? And with the seasonal transition right now, the scheduling is a total nightmare. I have three cashiers who can only work mornings because of daycare, and corporate just slashed our payroll hours again. I'm practically running the floor by myself half the time while trying to train people like Chloe. 

But, um, what were we talking about? Oh, right, trusting people. Yeah, like I said, I function totally fine and get along with people normally. The problems really only start when I get weird mail, or those constant bank calls, or when someone at work suddenly hands me "routine paperwork" that is very obviously tied to the whole plot with my house. That's when things get bad, because I can see how it's all connected. But otherwise? No, I handle my life and my job just fine.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a well-systematized, circumscribed persecutory delusion involving a coordinated conspiracy between their bank, loan servicer, and coworkers to cause foreclosure on their home, persisting for nearly two years. Hallucinations, passivity phenomena, and bizarre delusions are absent, and general functioning and personality outside the delusion are preserved, meeting criteria for Persistent Delusional Disorder (F22) while ruling out Schizophrenia and Paranoid Personality Disorder.
